minutes.headline: Board voted to direct its consultant to draft an MBTA Communities Act bylaw for the Tritown/Young's Road site.
minutes.summary: The Planning Board re-elected Matthew Brunner as chair, endorsed two ANR plans, and held two stormwater/site-plan public hearings (100 Townsend Harbor Road, approved; 260 Fuller Road, continued to July 14 pending peer review of contamination and drainage changes at a former dump site). It also voted to pursue "paper compliance" with the MBTA Communities Act at the Tritown apartment site and to reduce the Master Plan Steering Committee's quorum to five members.

budget_items.topic: 260 Fuller Road peer review fee (53G account)
budget_items.what_was_said: The board voted to require $2,000 deposited into a 53G account for peer review of the site plan/stormwater modification. There was discussion of whether an existing $4,000 already collected under a 'project review' line of the fee schedule could instead cover this, but the interim planner said that line has historically not been used for 53G peer review.
The chair said the town's fee schedule (dating to 2006) will get a full review once the town has a full-time planner in place; for now the board will continue handling fees the way it has been.

decisions.decision: Town manager confirmed the board can change the Master Plan Steering Committee's quorum requirement itself, and it does not need to stay above 50%.
Applicant for 100 Townsend Harbor Road made two requested changes (erosion control and spot grades/flow clarification) ahead of the hearing, reviewed by Graves Engineering.
Continuance date for 260 Fuller Road set for July 14, 2025 rather than a later date, partly to accommodate the review engineer's upcoming paternity leave.
Chair declined to sign the 443 West Townsend Road decision document without reviewing it first since it had not been received from the planner; signing deferred to the next meeting.
Board decided not to try to add the 443 West Townsend Road shared-driveway decision to the July 1 joint meeting with the select board, and to instead handle it at its next regular meeting.

what_happened.line: Board voted 3-0 to direct its consultant to draft an MBTA Communities Act bylaw for the Tritown/Young's Road site, the paper-compliance option.
The 260 Fuller Road warehouse site-plan hearing, over contamination and drainage at a former dump site, was continued to July 14 after a peer-review fee was assessed.
Board voted 3-0 to close the hearing and approve the stormwater permit for 100 Townsend Harbor Road with standard conditions.
Matthew Brunner was re-elected chair 3-1 after a first vote for Matthew Allison failed 1-3.
Board voted to lower the Master Plan Steering Committee's quorum to five members.

why_it_matters: The MBTA Communities Act vote sets which zoning path the town will pursue for multi-family housing near transit, ahead of a bylaw the town will eventually vote on.
The Fuller Road contamination and drainage questions bear on a warehouse project's approval and on water quality flowing toward Hickory Hills Lake.
A lower quorum makes it easier for the Master Plan Steering Committee to hold meetings and act going forward.
watch_next: Continued public hearing on 260 Fuller Road, July 14, 2025
Draft MBTA Communities Act bylaw from the board's consultant, Community Scale

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the main votes (both ANRs, the 100 Townsend-Harbor Rd approval, the July 14 continuance, MBTA Option B and the five-member quorum), allowing for caption misspellings of names and addresses. The official minutes are an unfinished draft with template placeholders, so they omit or differ on the chair election and the peer review wording. They also carry a stray 1083 Northfield Rd continuance vote and a blank attendance list, and a reader should check those against the recording.
